newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania c.bank says IMF backs currency plans.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania c.bank says IMF backs currency plans.

text.p: Lithuania's central bank chief Reinoldijus Sharkinas said on Tuesday that the International Monetary Fund (IMF) would support a more active monetary policy in Lithuania combined with keeping a fixed exchange rate.

Lithuania has a currency board system of keeping the litas currency fixed at four to one dollar, which means the central bank cannot influence monetary policy. The new government wants to scrap the board but keep a fixed peg, managed by the bank.
"The IMF fully supports...a more active participation of the central bank in monetary policy along with the preservation of a fixed litas rate," Sharkinas told Reuters in an interview.
Sharkinas earlier met an IMF mission visiting Lithuania.
"They (the IMF) understand our position, have seen the work we have done, and see that we can implement our plan to maintain the fixed exchange rate without the currency board," he said.
"The IMF was especially positive about the aspects of our programme in which we plan to keep the litas rate fixed to the US dollar," he added.
Under a currency board regime, the central bank guarantees that it will have a specific ratio of foreign funds in reserve to back the amount of local currency in circulation at the peg.
The new right-wing government which came to power last fall says it will scrap the currency board and return monetary policy tools to the central bank.

The IMF has said that it is ready to talk but will not support a hasty dismantling of the system. Under Lithuania's current memorandum with the Fund, the currency board must stay in place until Sem house in Malaysia
